::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Purpose"}
This assignment helps you choose visualizations that match the comparison you
want an audience to make and apply perception-aware design.

You will create exactly three visuals from different analytical frames and
justify the story, encoding, scope, and design choices for each one.
:::

## Objectives

By the end of this assignment, you will be able to:

- connect a data story to an appropriate analytical frame and chart type;
- apply clear scales, ordering, color, and labeling;
- state filters, units, and denominators; and
- explain why an encoding supports the intended comparison.

## Resources

- Week 3 slides on visual perception and analytical frames
- Week 1-2 slides on grain, NOIR, and descriptive summaries
- The four `.csv` files in the `data` folder
- Excel, Tableau, or R in Posit Cloud

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" icon="false" title="Expectations"}
Create exactly three visuals: one from Module A, one from Module B, and one from
Module C. Your grade emphasizes fit-for-purpose encodings, perceptual clarity,
and concise explanations.
:::

## 4) Visual B - Composition or Difference

Choose one frame:

- part-to-whole, shown as percentages that total 100%;
- a time series of one metric;
- deviation from a clearly labeled benchmark.

Use an honest baseline for a time series. Show a zero line and explain the
benchmark for deviation. Make the denominator explicit for part-to-whole.

## 5) Visual C - Distribution or Relationship

Choose one frame:

- a frequency distribution, such as a histogram or boxplot; or
- a relationship, such as a scatterplot with an optional trend line.

Use sensible bins, show units, reduce overplotting when needed, and identify
important outliers without allowing them to distort the scale.

## Optional R Example

If you choose to create a chart in R, adapt this scaffold. The example is not
executed because the variable names must be replaced with variables from your
dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(df, aes(x = your_category, y = your_value)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "A Takeaway-First Title",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Units"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

---

## 6) Review the Design

- [ ] Each chart matches its analytical frame.
- [ ] Axes, units, scales, and denominators are clear.
- [ ] Categories are ordered when order supports the story.
- [ ] Color is used sparingly and intentionally.
- [ ] The visuals avoid 3D effects and unnecessary decoration.
- [ ] Composition totals 100%, deviation shows zero, and relationships show
  appropriate scales when those frames are used.
- [ ] Each visual has concise alternative text.
